children.name: Campynema lineare Labill.
children.description: Campynema is a genus in the family Campynemataceae first described in 1805. It contains only one known species (monotypic), Campynema lineare, endemic to the island of Tasmania in Australia.

children.name: Campynemanthe neocaledonica  Goldblatt
children.description: Campynemanthe neocaledonica is a perennial herb or subshrub in the family Campynemataceae (Liliales), endemic to New Caledonia in the southwestern Pacific. It grows as a small, erect, rhizomatous herb with linear to lanceolate leaves and produces small greenish-yellow trimerous flowers in terminal inflorescences. The species is restricted to ultramafic substrates in wet montane forests of southern Grande Terre, occurring in shaded understory at mid-elevations. It represents part of an ancient Gondwanan lineage, one of the most primitive families within the lily order.

children.name: Campynemanthe parva Goldblatt
children.description: Campynemanthe parva is a perennial herb in the family Campynemataceae, described by Peter Goldblatt in 1986. It grows up to 50 cm tall and is distinguished by its elongated leaves. The species is endemic to southeastern New Caledonia, where it occurs in montane wet tropical forests on ultramafic substrates. Like other Campynemanthe species, it is a rhizomatous herb with linear leaves and small greenish trimerous flowers, and represents a relictual Gondwanan lineage within Liliales.

children.name: Campynemanthe viridiflora Baill.
children.description: Campynemanthe viridiflora is the type species of the genus Campynemanthe, first described by Henri Baillon in 1893. It is a perennial herb or subshrub 20–30 cm tall with distinctive greenish (viridulous) tepals and curved staminal filaments that give the genus its name. Endemic to New Caledonia, it occurs on serpentine substrates in wet montane forests of the southern part of Grande Terre, including Mount Mou. Like its congeners, it is a relictual monocot representing an early-diverging lineage within the order Liliales.
